radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate
Date: 24 January 2025
Facility: Catharina Ziekenhuis, Eindhoven
Clinical Indication: Rising PSA trajectory (5.8 ng/mL), follow-up mpMRI prostate.
FINDINGS:
The glandular volume measures 25.51 mL. T2-weighted sequences disclose a discrete hypointense focus within the right peripheral zone at the mid-gland level, spanning roughly 12 x 10 x 11 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging exhibits pronounced restriction, mirrored by corresponding hypointensity on the apparent diffusion coefficient map. Post-contrast dynamics demonstrate early, focal, and robust enhancement contrasting with adjacent parenchyma. Seminal vesicles remain unremarkable. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension or suspicious lymphadenopathy. The bladder and rectum appear structurally normal.
IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid-peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 25.51 mL; PSA density 0.227 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.87146586.

previous_notes.author: Dr. T. Hendriks (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical assessment occurred in September 2024 after May testing revealed a PSA elevation to 4.6 ng/mL. Given the persistent upward trend documented since 2022, multiparametric MRI was ordered and the patient was counseled regarding the trajectory. Urological follow-up was arranged while awaiting scan outcomes.
